200: I'm paid to teach forehands. Mostly I nod while people tell me about their week.
201: Today's lesson was one serve and forty minutes of talking about a fence.
202: I get more exercise fetching balls than my students get from hitting them.
203: Nobody comes here to learn tennis. They come to be listened to, near a net.
204: The ball machine never argues about the score. It is my favorite student.
205: We warm up for ten minutes and play for two. Stretching is the whole sport now.
206: I fix their grip, they thank me warmly, then hold it exactly as wrong as before.
207: Two hours on the court today. I hit maybe four balls. Heard about four hundred things.
208: We take a water break every four minutes. Hydration has become the real workout.
209: I could teach a wall. The wall would at least stay on its side of the net.
210: I run to every corner of the court so my students can stand still and watch.
211: They pay me to improve their game, then spend the whole hour explaining why today doesn't count.
212: I keep score for people who stopped playing twenty minutes ago.
213: My best students are the ones who occasionally remember there's a ball.
214: I demonstrate a perfect swing. Nobody watches. Everybody claps anyway.
215: New racket, new shoes, a matching outfit. The actual swing arrives whenever it feels ready.
216: I used to say 'bend your knees.' The knees and I have quietly agreed to stop.
217: Some days I'm a coach. Most days I'm a friend who happens to own a net.
218: They dress for a championship, then spend an hour hunting for the ball in a bush.
219: I supply the balls, the rackets, and the encouragement. Mostly they misplace the balls.
220: People tell me their deepest secrets. By closing time I've forgotten every one.
221: People ask me for advice. I offer a napkin and a glass of water. Same result, honestly.
222: Everyone assumes I remember them. I remember the drink. Never the story.
223: One man has ordered the exact same drink for years. I deeply admire the commitment.
224: Someone returned a drink for having one too few olives. I added three. Peace was restored.
225: A man told me his whole life last night. I nodded. I retained the ice request.
226: People think I'm wise. I'm just standing still while they talk.
227: I know everything about everyone here, for exactly the length of one glass.
228: At the end of the night I call last orders, and everyone suddenly has much more to say.
229: My memory holds two things: the specials, and absolutely none of your secrets.
230: I've been told forty personal crises this week. Ask me one. I dare you.
231: The tip jar and I have the same job tonight: sitting here, looking hopeful, staying almost empty.
232: A customer wanted water, but fancier. I served it in a nicer glass. They were delighted.
233: Someone told me a huge secret an hour ago. It was, I'm sure, a very good one.
234: The bar is the safest place in town. I couldn't testify to anything.
235: I remember every order. I forget every heartbreak. It's a useful arrangement.
236: I wipe the same glass clean forty times a night. It gives my hands something to do.
237: My hardest task is telling a very happy person that they have had quite enough happiness.
238: A regular tells me the same long story every week. I have started to enjoy the ending.
239: I've recited today's specials three hundred times. By now I believe in them completely.
